x: Graham, Martin and Andy showed the sort of backing which could give them a place medal in the Southern and possibly the National Junior races when Matt and Justin Chaston come into the team.

Phil' Idowu, Austin Ferns, Marlon Dickson, Chris' Lambert, Marlon Kerr, Charles Igbon, Samson Oni, Matt' Russell, Darren Thompson... All of these and more athletes have enjoyed regular appearances in our showcase team either in League or Cup contests.
Meanwhile, Matt' Russell was seeing how best he could traumatise his coach as well as himself in the senior 100m after he failed to make an impression on the leaders of his heat.
Matt Douglas and Chris Rawlinson successfully moved through the heats of the 400 metres hurdles in spite of the howling gale against them in the back straight.

Matt Douglas set the required standard in winning the 400 metres hurdles and Darren Campbell matched this in the 100 metres. Among the next results, the discus found Kevin Brown in 2nd which was better than expected and Phillips Idowu was only 16 centimetres short of his best in winning the triple j…

Matt Douglas made a welcome return and looked forward to contesting the opening track event with Duaine Ladejo. Both considered themselves Olympic contenders for the 400mH and were looking for a qualifying time.

Matt Douglas did the high jump and both relays. Neil Owen added the hammer to his repertoire and when asked by the judge whether he was a right or left handed thrower, said that he preferred the central delivery.
In the men’s 400m hurdles, Matt Douglas also made it to the semi-finals, having spent almost the whole of 2005 on the sidelines through a back injury.

It was back in 1987 that we last lined up a Junior Men’s squad – four to a team in those days, when the race was held at Crystal Palace – and we placed 7th with Matt and Justin Chaston, Matt Kinane and Glen Tiernan.
Matt was lying about 20th at half way but the wheels came off when the course swung onto a shingle beach at about 15miles where he lost a lot of places!
